Hellship Casualty Roster

Compiled reference · 8,370 records
10 Japanese "hellship" sinkings, 1942–1944

A searchable roster of Allied prisoners of war carried aboard Japanese transport ships torpedoed or bombed by Allied forces unaware of their human cargo, along with the men who survived those sinkings.

About this roster and its sources

This roster merges casualty and survivor lists for ten hellships — Arisan Maru, Oryoku Maru, Junyo Maru, Lisbon Maru, Hofuku Maru, Shinyo Maru, Montevideo Maru, Rakuyo Maru, Kachidoki Maru, and Brazil Maru — drawn from sources including COFEPOW, the Roll of Honour (UK), and Japansekrijgsgevangenkampen.nl, among others cited per record where available.

Some historical facts remain genuinely disputed among primary sources (for instance, the submarine that sank Arisan Maru), and a number of fields are sparse simply because no record survives. Where a value was reconstructed, standardized, or flagged as uncertain during compilation, that is preserved in the record's Data Quality note rather than silently corrected. Two mass casualty events are undercounted here by nature of the surviving record: the roughly 4,200 Javanese rōmusha forced laborers aboard Junyo Maru, and 90 additional Lisbon Maru dead in the weeks after its sinking, have no name-level source and are not included.

Click any row for the full record, including notes, memorial/burial site, and source link where known.
